PHIL 101.description: Topics selected by the instructor for specialized study. Course content varies and will be announced in the schedule of classes by title.
PHIL 101.subject: PHIL
PHIL 101.title: Special Topics in Philosophy

PHIL 102.description: An introduction to the main problems of philosophy and its methods of inquiry, analysis, and criticism. Works of important philosophers will be read. Honors section offered.
PHIL 102.subject: PHIL
PHIL 102.title: Introduction to Philosophy

PHIL 103.description: A study of the moral principles of conduct and the basic concepts underlying these principles, such as good, evil, right, wrong, justice, value, duty, and obligation, as they relate to specific issues or areas of life. May be repeated as content varies by title.
PHIL 103.subject: PHIL
PHIL 103.title: Special Topics in Ethics and Values

PHIL 111.description: Philosophical foundations of inductive inference, including probability, statistics, and decision theory; application of the methods and results of inductive inference to philosophical problems such as the problem of rationality, epistemology, theory confirmation, social and political philosophy.
PHIL 111.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: At least one of the following: PSYC 227; SOCY 220; STAT 110, STAT 112, STAT 201, STAT 205, or STAT 206; MGSC 291.
PHIL 111.subject: PHIL
PHIL 111.title: Introduction to Logic II

PHIL 114.description: Formal logic, including foundational logical concepts, syntax and semantics of first-order logic; derivations; applications.
PHIL 114.subject: PHIL
PHIL 114.title: Introduction to Formal Logic I

PHIL 115.description: Intermediate topics in predicate logic, including second-order predicate logic; meta-theory, including soundness and completeness; introduction to non-classical logic
PHIL 115.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or higher in PHIL114 or PHIL 110, or a department-approved equivalent.
PHIL 115.subject: PHIL
PHIL 115.title: Introduction to Formal Logic II

PHIL 210.description: Selected philosophical problems as they are presented in imaginative and theoretical literature. Works of fiction and philosophical treatments of issues involved in them will be read and discussed.
PHIL 210.subject: PHIL
PHIL 210.title: Philosophical Themes in Literature

PHIL 211.description: Moral issues confronting men and women in contemporary society. Topics will vary but may include discussion of problems related to abortion, drugs, euthanasia, war, social engineering, and punishment of criminals.
PHIL 211.subject: PHIL
PHIL 211.title: Contemporary Moral Issues

PHIL 212.description: Images of the human person in contemporary philosophy, literature, psychology, and religion, and an evaluation of these images as norms for human conduct and social policy. Particular attention may be given to images found in specific philosophical traditions, including existentialism, Marxism, behaviorism, and mysticism.
PHIL 212.subject: PHIL
PHIL 212.title: Images of the Human Person

PHIL 213.description: Moral issues confronting men and women in contemporary society and the challenges of communicating effectively about them. Topics will vary but may include access to health care, euthanasia, abortion, same sex marriage and the moral and environmental consequences of eating animals.
PHIL 213.subject: PHIL
PHIL 213.title: Communicating Moral Issues

PHIL 214.description: Attempts to distinguish science from pseudo-science; inquiry into such cases as astrology, psychoanalysis, and parapsychology.
PHIL 214.subject: PHIL
PHIL 214.title: Science and Pseudo-Science

PHIL 220.description: An immersive introduction to the nature and function of law, with special emphasis on the interpretation and application of the law in the judicial process. Readings in classical and contemporary philosophy of law will be considered.
PHIL 220.subject: PHIL
PHIL 220.title: Philosophy of Law

PHIL 301.description: An introduction to the work of ancient philosophers, with special emphasis on Plato and Aristotle.
PHIL 301.subject: PHIL
PHIL 301.title: Ancient Philosophy

PHIL 302.description: Problems such as hedonism, providence, belief and evidence, and mysticism, as they appear in the writings of Epicureans, Stoics, Skeptics, and Plotinus.
PHIL 302.subject: PHIL
PHIL 302.title: Greek and Roman Philosophy after Aristotle

PHIL 303.description: Major philosophical traditions in the Middle Ages.
PHIL 303.subject: PHIL
PHIL 303.title: History of Medieval Philosophy

PHIL 304.description: An introduction to Continental and British philosophy running roughly from Descartes through Kant.
PHIL 304.subject: PHIL
PHIL 304.title: Seventeenth and Eighteenth-Century Philosophy

PHIL 305.description: An introduction to Continental and British philosophy since Kant through study of the works of representative philosophers. Particular emphasis is placed on the development of Idealism, Marxism, Existentialism and Phenomenology, and analytic philosophy.
PHIL 305.subject: PHIL
PHIL 305.title: Nineteenth and Twentieth-Century Philosophy

PHIL 310.description: The principal movements of philosophical thought from Colonial times to the present, with special emphasis on the 19th and 20th centuries.
PHIL 310.subject: PHIL
PHIL 310.title: American Philosophy

PHIL 311.description: An introduction to existentialist themes in contemporary philosophy, literature, psychology, and religion. The writings of existentialists such as Kierkegaard, Nietzsche, Camus, Sartre, Buber, May, and Binswanger will be read and discussed.
PHIL 311.subject: PHIL
PHIL 311.title: Existentialism

PHIL 312.description: Examination of ancient Greek and Roman philosophical, medical, and literary works (in English) as sources for the origins of medical ethics. Priority enrollment for Medical Humanities students.
PHIL 312.subject: PHIL
PHIL 312.title: Classical Origins of Western Medical Ethics

PHIL 313.description: Introduction to ancient medicine: science and art, theory and practice, healing and predicting. Topics include Medicine before Hippocrates, Hippocratic medicine, holism, naturalism, medicine, religion and magic, medicine and scientific explanation, Hellenistic medicine and methodology, Galenic medicine.
PHIL 313.subject: PHIL
PHIL 313.title: Between Magic and Method: Ancient Medicine

PHIL 315.description: A historical overview and critical introduction to the philosophical practices of Asian religions; an examination of the basic worldviews, thought frameworks, and foundational questions of the main schools of premodern Asian religious philosophy.
PHIL 315.subject: PHIL
PHIL 315.title: Asian Religious Philosophy

PHIL 320.description: A study of the moral principles of conduct and the basic concepts underlying these principles, such as good, evil, right, wrong, justice, value, duty, and obligation. The ethical works of influential philosophers are analyzed in terms of these concepts.
PHIL 320.subject: PHIL
PHIL 320.title: Ethics

PHIL 321.description: The concepts of Person and Justice as they relate to biomedical sciences and technologies.
PHIL 321.subject: PHIL
PHIL 321.title: Medical Ethics

PHIL 322.description: Examination of principles and arguments surrounding moral issues involving the environment.
PHIL 322.subject: PHIL
PHIL 322.title: Environmental Ethics

PHIL 323.description: Role of ethical judgments in directing or curtailing scientific research; case studies from natural and social sciences.
PHIL 323.subject: PHIL
PHIL 323.title: Ethics of Science and Technology

PHIL 324.description: Ethical problems in business; application to business situations of philosophical theories of individual, corporate, and governmental rights and responsibilities.
PHIL 324.subject: PHIL
PHIL 324.title: Business Ethics

PHIL 325.description: An investigation of ethical issues in engineering and engineering-related technology. Topics include whistleblowing, employee/employer relations, environmental issues, issues related to advances in information technology, and privacy.
PHIL 325.subject: PHIL
PHIL 325.title: Engineering Ethics

PHIL 326.description: Moral concepts such as justice, privacy, and equality applied to artificial intelligence technologies.
PHIL 326.subject: PHIL
PHIL 326.title: AI Ethics

PHIL 329.description: An examination and critical assessment of the philosophical concepts, issues, and questions surrounding the relationship of church and state.
PHIL 329.subject: PHIL
PHIL 329.title: Law and Religion

PHIL 330.description: An overview of major themes in political philosophy such as the nature of politics, obligation, community, representation, freedom, equality, and justice.
PHIL 330.subject: PHIL
PHIL 330.title: Social and Political Philosophy

PHIL 331.description: The fundamental concepts of a criminal justice system and their philosophical bases. Rights, privacy, responsibility, and the problem of justification of state control of private behavior through punishment and therapy.
PHIL 331.subject: PHIL
PHIL 331.title: Crime and Justice

PHIL 332.description: A critical examination of the theories of education of such philosophers as Plato, Rousseau, Dewey, Newman, and Whitehead. Emphasis is on the development of a philosophy of higher education.
PHIL 332.subject: PHIL
PHIL 332.title: Philosophy of Education

PHIL 333.description: Recent Marxist-inspired critics of politics, science, technology, art, advertising, and other aspects of cultural life, with comparison both to Marx’s philosophical and economic writings and to other types of contemporary criticisms.
PHIL 333.subject: PHIL
PHIL 333.title: Contemporary Marxism and Society

PHIL 334.description: Introduces feminist philosophy and applications to philosophical problems.
PHIL 334.subject: PHIL
PHIL 334.title: Feminist Philosophy

PHIL 335.description: This course explores central philosophical issues related to resisting and opposing claimed state authority. Focus will be on classic and modern texts regarding the intentional, ethically-, or politically-motivated violation of law and on the justification of revolution.
PHIL 335.subject: PHIL
PHIL 335.title: Disobedience, Dissent, and Revolution

PHIL 340.description: Philosophical problems relating to the arts, the nature of artworks, artistic meaning, aesthetic experience, and artistic values.
PHIL 340.subject: PHIL
PHIL 340.title: Philosophy of Art

PHIL 341.description: Selected philosophical problems as they are presented in feature and documentary films.
PHIL 341.subject: PHIL
PHIL 341.title: Philosophy and Film

PHIL 350.description: Examination of skeptical attacks, critical defenses, and philosophical theories of what we know and what is to be taken as ultimate reality.
PHIL 350.subject: PHIL
PHIL 350.title: Knowledge and Reality

PHIL 351.description: Philosophical theories about the nature of consciousness, the problem of qualia, phenomenal concepts, the explanatory gap hypothesis, higher-order consciousness, prospects for naturalistic accounts of consciousness.
PHIL 351.subject: PHIL
PHIL 351.title: Mind and Nature

PHIL 352.description: An examination of the nature of human action, agency, ability, intentions, reason, and free will.
PHIL 352.subject: PHIL
PHIL 352.title: Feedom and Human Action

PHIL 360.description: Philosophy and history of science and their interaction from ancient Greece to the present. Emphasis on physics, astronomy, and chemistry.
PHIL 360.subject: PHIL
PHIL 360.title: History and Philosophy of Science

PHIL 363.description: Historical, ethical and epistemic development of science and technology in its relationship to society.
PHIL 363.subject: PHIL
PHIL 363.title: Science, Technology and Society

PHIL 365.description: Formal theories of rationality in the context of decision-making and games; uses of these formal theories to address traditional philosophical issues such as rationality, knowledge, choice, social welfare, cooperation, and communication.
PHIL 365.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or higher in any course that satisfies the ARP Carolina Core requirement.
PHIL 365.subject: PHIL
PHIL 365.title: Formal Theories of Rationality and Their Philosophical Implications

PHIL 370.description: Topics selected by the instructor for specialized study. Course content varies and will be announced in the schedule of classes by title.
PHIL 370.subject: PHIL
PHIL 370.title: Special Topics in Philosophy

PHIL 371.description: Writing-intensive study in philosophy of the pre-modern period. Course content varies and will be announced in the schedule of classes by title. As a writing-intensive course, substantial time will be devoted to developing and improving the student’s ability to write clear, well-reasoned, and compelling philosophical essays.
PHIL 371.subject: PHIL
PHIL 371.title: Writing-Intensive: Ancient Philosophy

PHIL 372.description: Writing-intensive study in philosophy of the modern period. Course content varies and will be announced in the schedule of classes by title. As a writing-intensive course, substantial time will be devoted to developing and improving the student’s ability to write clear, well-reasoned, and compelling philosophical essays.
PHIL 372.subject: PHIL
PHIL 372.title: Writing-Intensive: Modern Philosophy

PHIL 373.description: Writing-intensive study in one or more fields of philosophy. Course content varies and will be announced in the schedule of classes by title. As a writing-intensive course, substantial time will be devoted to developing and improving the student’s ability to write clear, well-reasoned, and compelling philosophical essays.
PHIL 373.subject: PHIL
PHIL 373.title: Writing-Intensive: Field of Philosophy

PHIL 390.description: Overview of philosophical theories and debates with attention to skills in discussion and presentation and in preparing and writing a research paper in philosophy. Topics selected by the instructor.
PHIL 390.subject: PHIL
PHIL 390.title: Junior Seminar in Philosophy

PHIL 399.description: Contract approved by instructor, advisor, and department chair is required for undergraduate students.
PHIL 399.subject: PHIL
PHIL 399.title: Independent Study

PHIL 490.description: Review of central topics in philosophy serving as a capstone course for senior majors in philosophy.
PHIL 490.subject: PHIL
PHIL 490.title: Senior Seminar in Philosophy

PHIL 495.description: Directed research resulting in a written thesis. Senior philosophy major or double major, GPA of 3.30, permission of faculty member.
PHIL 495.subject: PHIL
PHIL 495.title: Senior Thesis

PHIL 499.description: Supervised professional experience or research outside the classroom, involving a meaningful project or activity for the employing firm or organization and a scholarly project for the student. An Undergraduate Internship Contract is required.
PHIL 499.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: B or higher in two PHIL courses numbered 300 or above.
PHIL 499.subject: PHIL
PHIL 499.title: Internship in Philosophy

PHIL 501.description: A historical and critical survey of the British philosophers of experience. Principal concentration is on Locke, Berkeley, and Hume.
PHIL 501.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in PHIL 304.
PHIL 501.subject: PHIL
PHIL 501.title: British Empiricism

PHIL 502.description: A critical and historical study of the 17th-century European philosophers. The works of Descartes, Spinoza, and Leibniz are emphasized.
PHIL 502.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in PHIL 304.
PHIL 502.subject: PHIL
PHIL 502.title: Continental Rationalism

PHIL 503.description: A critical study of recent and contemporary works in philosophical analysis, and an evaluation of the purposes, methods, and results of this movement.
PHIL 503.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better on 3 hours in philosophy beyond the 100 level.
PHIL 503.subject: PHIL
PHIL 503.title: Analytic Philosophy

PHIL 504.description: A critical study of some fundamental themes in phenomenology and the philosophy of existence. Emphasis is placed on an intensive study of selected works of such writers as Kierkegaard, Jaspers, Husserl, and Heidegger.
PHIL 504.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in PHIL 304 or PHIL 305.
PHIL 504.subject: PHIL
PHIL 504.title: Phenomenology and Existentialism

PHIL 505.description: An intensive study of selected Dialogues by Plato.
PHIL 505.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in PHIL 301.
PHIL 505.subject: PHIL
PHIL 505.title: Plato

PHIL 506.description: An intensive study of some of the more important of Aristotle's works.
PHIL 506.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in PHIL 301.
PHIL 506.subject: PHIL
PHIL 506.title: Aristotle

PHIL 507.description: A historical and critical study of the works of the leading medieval philosophers.
PHIL 507.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in PHIL 303.
PHIL 507.subject: PHIL
PHIL 507.title: Medieval Philosophy

PHIL 508.description: An intensive study of the philosophical writings of Hume, especially A Treatise of Human Nature.
PHIL 508.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in PHIL 304.
PHIL 508.subject: PHIL
PHIL 508.title: Hume

PHIL 509.description: An intensive study of the work of Kant, especially the Critique of Pure Reason.
PHIL 509.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in PHIL 304.
PHIL 509.subject: PHIL
PHIL 509.title: Kant

PHIL 510.description: An examination of some representative theories of truth, meaning, probability, and perception.
PHIL 510.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in 3 hours in philosophy beyond the 100 level.
PHIL 510.subject: PHIL
PHIL 510.title: Theory of Knowledge

PHIL 511.description: A presentation and philosophical examination of the fundamentals of modern symbolic logic.
PHIL 511.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in PHIL 115.
PHIL 511.subject: PHIL
PHIL 511.title: Symbolic Logic

PHIL 512.description: A critical examination of methods and concepts of the sciences. Topics include scientific revolutions, the unity of science, experimentation, explanation, and evidence.
PHIL 512.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in 3 hours in philosophy beyond the 100 level.
PHIL 512.subject: PHIL
PHIL 512.title: Philosophy of Science

PHIL 513.description: A philosophical examination of historical inquiry. Theories of historical development. The logical problems of historical explanation.
PHIL 513.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in 3 hours in philosophy beyond the 100 level.
PHIL 513.subject: PHIL
PHIL 513.title: Philosophy of History

PHIL 514.description: Survey of recent and historical developments in ethical theory with special emphasis on the meaning of ethical language and the forms of reasoning employed in discussing moral values.
PHIL 514.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in PHIL 320.
PHIL 514.subject: PHIL
PHIL 514.title: Ethical Theory

PHIL 515.description: A critical study of selected problems in the philosophy of religion. Emphasis is placed on problems relating to the existence of God, religious knowledge, and the language of religion.
PHIL 515.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in 3 hours in philosophy beyond the 100 level.
PHIL 515.subject: PHIL
PHIL 515.title: Philosophy of Religion

PHIL 516.description: Detailed examination of the literature on aesthetics.
PHIL 516.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in 3 hours in philosophy beyond the 100 level.
PHIL 516.subject: PHIL
PHIL 516.title: Advanced Aesthetics

PHIL 517.description: An examination of concepts and problems such as meaning, reference, analyticity, definition, and the relation between logic and philosophy.
PHIL 517.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or higher in PHIL 114 or PHIL 511.
PHIL 517.subject: PHIL
PHIL 517.title: Philosophy of Language

PHIL 518.description: The goals of inquiry and problems such as objectivity, reduction, value freedom, and ideology.
PHIL 518.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in 3 hours in philosophy beyond the 100 level.
PHIL 518.subject: PHIL
PHIL 518.title: Philosophy of the Social Sciences

PHIL 519.description: Major issues in classical and modern metaphysics. Topics include the idea of first philosophy, being, substance, the problem of universals, essentialism, causation, time and space, and metaphysical method.
PHIL 519.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in PHIL 350 or PHIL 351 or PHIL 360.
PHIL 519.subject: PHIL
PHIL 519.title: Metaphysics

PHIL 520.description: The concept of mind, the mind-body problem, emotions and cognition, the possibility of artificial minds, theories of embodied cognition.
PHIL 520.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in PHIL 350 or PHIL 351 or PHIL 360.
PHIL 520.subject: PHIL
PHIL 520.title: Philosophy of Mind

PHIL 521.description: Axiomatic development of logic and the set-theoretic foundations of mathematics.
PHIL 521.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in PHIL 511.
PHIL 521.subject: PHIL
PHIL 521.title: Mathematical Logic

PHIL 522.description: Introduction to the study of linguistic meaning, including the following topics: meaning, reference, and truth; the connections among language, thought, and reality; word meaning and sentence meaning; possible worlds and modality; thematic roles; meaning and context; presupposition and implicature; speech acts; formal semantics; and cognitive semantics.
PHIL 522.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in any of LING 300, LING 301, LING 600, PHIL 114, PHIL 511.
PHIL 522.subject: PHIL
PHIL 522.title: Introduction to Semantics and Pragmatics

PHIL 523.description: Philosophical problems about logic, the development of philosophical logics, and the problems surrounding them.
PHIL 523.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in PHIL 511.
PHIL 523.subject: PHIL
PHIL 523.title: Advanced Topics in Logic

PHIL 524.description: Examination of major conceptual, theoretical, and methodological issues in biological science. Topics include reductionism, units of selection, adaptationism, relations between evolutionary and developmental biology and between biology and society.
PHIL 524.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in 3 hours of Philosophy beyond the 100 level.
PHIL 524.subject: PHIL
PHIL 524.title: Philosophy of Biology

PHIL 526.description: Survey of the major schools and trends in Hellenistic philosophy: Epicureans, Stoics, Academic Skeptics. Topics include eudaimonism, hedonism, monism, teleology, and the criterion of truth.
PHIL 526.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in PHIL 301 or PHIL 302.
PHIL 526.subject: PHIL
PHIL 526.title: Hellenistic Philosophy

PHIL 527.description: Recent contributions to three central strands of ethical theory: virtue theory, deontology, and utilitarianism; historical roots and recent developments.
PHIL 527.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in PHIL 320.
PHIL 527.subject: PHIL
PHIL 527.title: Virtues, Acts, and Consequences

PHIL 528.description: Systematic approaches to data analysis--Bayesian, Fisherian and decision theoretic--will be critically appraised. Applications of these theories to some problems of inductive logic: the paradoxes of confirmation, the role of simplicity, and the probability of inductive generalizations.
PHIL 528.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in PHIL 350 or PHIL 351 or PHIL 360.
PHIL 528.subject: PHIL
PHIL 528.title: Concepts of Evidence

PHIL 531.description: An examination of a number of philosophical problems about the law: the nature and function of rules, the difference between legal rules and other rules, the nature of reasoning from legal rules, the concept of a legal system, and the relation of law and morals.
PHIL 531.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in PHIL 320 or PHIL 330.
PHIL 531.subject: PHIL
PHIL 531.title: Jurisprudence

PHIL 532.description: Recent theories of distributive justice and their application to such issues as redistribution of wealth, reverse discrimination, and the conflict between liberty and equality. Authors include Rawls, Nozick, Hayek, and Popper.
PHIL 532.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in PHIL 320 or PHIL 321 or PHIL 322 or PHIL 330 or PHIL 331.
PHIL 532.subject: PHIL
PHIL 532.title: Social Justice

PHIL 534.description: An examination of European social philosophy associated with either the Frankfurt School of Social Research or contemporary French Poststructuralism.
PHIL 534.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in 3 hours in philosophy beyond the 100 level.
PHIL 534.subject: PHIL
PHIL 534.title: Contemporary European Social Philosophy

PHIL 535.description: An exploration of the connections between oppression of women and oppression of nature.
PHIL 535.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: 3 hours in philosophy beyond the 100 level.
PHIL 535.subject: PHIL
PHIL 535.title: Ecofeminism

PHIL 536.description: Selected contemporary European philosophical movements, their views on language, and their approach to interpretation: hermeneutics, structuralism, poststructuralism.
PHIL 536.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in PHIL 114.
PHIL 536.subject: PHIL
PHIL 536.title: Language and Interpretation in Contemporary European Philosophy

PHIL 540.description: Humanism (e.g., Petrarca), Platonism (e.g., Pico and Ficino), Aristotelianism (e.g., Pomponazzi), philosophies of nature (e.g., Telesio, Campanella, and Bruno), and Nicholas of Cusa, Erasmus, Montaigne, and Suarez.
PHIL 540.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in PHIL 301 or PHIL 302 or PHIL 303.
PHIL 540.subject: PHIL
PHIL 540.title: Renaissance Philosophy

PHIL 550.description: An exploration of the ethical dimensions of patient care in the clinical setting.
PHIL 550.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in PHIL 320 or PHIL 321 or PHIL 322 or PHIL 330 or PHIL 331.
PHIL 550.subject: PHIL
PHIL 550.title: Health Care Ethics

PHIL 560.description: Advanced special topics in Philosophy. May be repeated as content varies by title.
PHIL 560.subject: PHIL
PHIL 560.title: Advanced Special Topics in Philosophy

PHIL 598.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: 6 hours in philosophy beyond the 100 level.
PHIL 598.subject: PHIL
PHIL 598.title: Readings in Philosophy

PHIL 706.description: Study of the works of one or more major contemporary continental philosophers.
PHIL 706.subject: PHIL
PHIL 706.title: Studies in Continental Philosophy

PHIL 710.description: Students are introduced to formal and informal codes of professional conduct of various health science disciplines and understand the implications of these distinctions for interdisciplinary research, clinical practice, and administration.
PHIL 710.subject: PHIL
PHIL 710.title: Ethics and the Health Sciences

PHIL 715.description: Classic and contemporary theories of ethics and their applications to criminal justice decision-making.
PHIL 715.subject: PHIL
PHIL 715.title: Ethics in Criminal Justice

PHIL 716.description: Topics and problems arising in the philosophy of mind.
PHIL 716.subject: PHIL
PHIL 716.title: Philosophy of Mind

PHIL 717.description: Study of formal approaches to pragmatic phenomena such as focus, presupposition, and implicature; examination of deictic, contextual and perspectival expressions; survey of pragmatic frameworks such as Relevance Theory and Discourse Representation Theory; study of information structural properties of natural languages, including topic- comment structure, given-new contrasts, definiteness versus indefiniteness.
PHIL 717.subject: PHIL
PHIL 717.title: Pragmatic Theory

PHIL 718.description: Examination of concepts such as meaning, reference, analyticity, and translational indeterminacy; evaluation of accounts of speech acts, the semantics of propositional attitudes, and metaphor and other pragmatic phenomena.
PHIL 718.subject: PHIL
PHIL 718.title: Studies in Philosophy of Language

PHIL 719.description: The formal study of linguistic meaning, including the following topics: Fregean truth-conditional semantics; lexical decomposition; predication and modification; lambda abstraction; generalized quantification; intentional and extensional contexts; tense, aspect, and modality; propositional attitudes; and indexicality.
PHIL 719.subject: PHIL
PHIL 719.title: Semantic Theory

PHIL 735.description: Recent work in philosophy regarding political and social values, principles of justice, political quthority, institutions, and related subjects.
PHIL 735.subject: PHIL
PHIL 735.title: Contemporary Political Philosophy

PHIL 763.description: Survey of historical and recent trends in epistemology.
PHIL 763.subject: PHIL
PHIL 763.title: Epistemology

PHIL 764.description: Survey of historical and recent trends in metaphysics.
PHIL 764.subject: PHIL
PHIL 764.title: Metaphysics

PHIL 767.description: Introduction to the method of studying historical cases in the philosophy of science. This course revolves around the sustained treatment of one or two such cases.
PHIL 767.subject: PHIL
PHIL 767.title: Case Study in the Philosophy of Science

PHIL 790.description: Materials, techniques, and problems of teaching philosophy. Repeatable for credit.
PHIL 790.subject: PHIL
PHIL 790.title: Teaching Philosophy

PHIL 798.description: Student and faculty presentations of current research in specified subject areas. Content varies. May be repeated for credit.
PHIL 798.subject: PHIL
PHIL 798.title: Research Seminar

PHIL 835.description: Examination of the intellectual, cultural, and ethical frameworks within which environmental problems arise and are solved.
PHIL 835.subject: PHIL
PHIL 835.title: Seminar in Environmental Ethics

PHIL 847.description: Critical comparison of present-day schools of thought in the nature, objectives, and functions of American education.
PHIL 847.subject: PHIL
PHIL 847.title: Modern Philosophies of Education
